1
Judgment
The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 21.04.2023 at about 9.00 p.m. the petitioner was proceeding in his motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-KC-6812 from Tank bund Road on KSRTC Service Road,
Kempegowda Bus Stand, Majestic, near KSRTC Terminal Exit Gate-2, at that time,
driver of KSRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-37- F-0821 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Srinivasa Hospital, Bengaluru, after first aid treatment he was shifted to Promed Hospital wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and by spending Rs.4,50,000/- towards medical expenses,
conveyance and nourishment food etc.,
3.

It is stated that prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 45 years and working as a clerk in S.Anil Kumar Advocate, at M.Shivappa Associates, Bengaluru and earning 25,000/- p.m. and contributing the same towards maintenance of his family.
Due to accidental injuries, he could not able to his activities as earlier.
4. It is stated that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-37-F-0821.
Hence, the Upparpet Police have registered criminal case against driver of the offending vehicle in Crime No.152/2023 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 of IPC.
As such, the respondents are liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.
5. Inspite of service of notice, respondent No.2 has appeared through it's counsel and filed the written statement.

On the other hand, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this tribunal,
remained absent, placed exparte.
6. In the written statement of the respondent No.2 has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
Ultimately stated that the claim of the petitioner is highly excessive, exaggerated and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.

7. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
ISSUES

Rudresha D E vs Ksrtc on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92222954/
2

1. Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident which is result of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-37-F-0821?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, at what rate and from whom?
3.
What order
or award?
8. In order to substantiate his case, the petitioner got examined himself as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P20.

Apart from his evidence placed the evidence of Dr.Peddi Manjunath as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P21 to Ex.P23.
9.

On the other hand, the respondents got examined its driver as RW1 and got marked documents as Ex.R1.
10.
Heard the arguments of both the counsel and perused the materials available on record.

11. My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3:

As per final order,
 for the following:
 R E A S O N S ISSUE NO.1:-
12.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA- 37-F-0821, the alleged accident had taken place, consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.

13. On the contrary, the respondent though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, but strongly disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC bus.
In such a situation, burden is more on the part of the petitioner, to prove the above issues on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
14. The petitioner in order to prove his case, petitioner examined himself as PW1.
In his examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
PW1 in support of his oral evidence has relied upon Ex.P1 to Ex.P7.
Ex . P1
-true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.152/2023 of Upparpet Police Station.
Ex. P2- true copy of first information statement given by Rudresha D E vs Ksrtc on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92222954/
3 petitioner.
Ex. P3-true copy spot mahazar, Ex.P4-true copy of spot sketch, Ex.P5- IMV report, Ex.P6- wound certificate, Ex.P7-true copy of charge sheet.

15. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by petitioner, the S.H.O. of Upparpet police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 337 of I.P.C.
Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.
16. On the contrary, driver of the KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-37-F-0821 was examined as RW1.

He has strongly contended that, he was proceeding towards Totadappa Chowltary from Tank Bund Road, on KBS Service Road to park the bus, at that point of time, the petitioner came on a motor cycle bearing No.KA-02-KC-6812 from behind by riding the same in a rash and negligent manner with high speed in order to over take the bus from the left side, tried to sneak between the Bus and Auto rickshaw, but there was no sufficient space between the bus and Auto rickshaw and there was heavy raining, totally last control over the motor cycle and fell down on his right side and exposed himself for the alleged accident.
Hence, he is no way responsible for the cause of accident.
To prove the defenses of the respondent, he has placed police endrorsement which is marked at Ex.R1.
On perusal of Ex.R1 it appears that he sent a letter dated 22.04.2023 to CPI, Upparpet Traffic Police Station through post.
In reply to said letter the police have issued Ex.R1 stating that investigation is continuing.
RW-1 have not given complaint on the date of accident.
It appears that only to over come from the allegation he send a letter.
Apart from this there is no convincing materials available on record for consideration.
Even in the cross-examination, no material points are forthcoming to disbelieve the case of the petitioner.

17. Apart from this, at the time of cross- examination of PW1, no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondent about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle.
18. In the light of the evidence placed by petitioner, I am of the view that, the petitioner has placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing No.KA-37-F-0821 and in the said accident, petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2:
19.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

20. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.

Rudresha D E vs Ksrtc on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92222954/
4
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India

. 
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.
The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

"while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P6.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
Right leg is crush and degloving injury of skin around ankel and heal pad with fracture of medial malleolus and fifth metatarsal.
22.
In connection with the above said injuries are grievous in nature.
Further, the petitioner has produced discharge summaries and x-ray as per Ex.P9, Ex.P10 and Ex.P17.
On perusal of discharge summary marked at Ex.P9 & 10 shows that the petitioner was admitted from 21.04.2023 to 02.05.2023 and 31.05.2023 to 05.06.2023.
In addition to his evidence placed the evidence of Dr.Peddi Manjunath as PW2.
He has deposed that the petitioner has sustained Right leg are crush and degloving injury of skin around ankel and heal pad with fracture of medial malleolus and firth metatarsla.
He has placed case sheets and outpatient record at Ex.P21 to Ex.P23.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.60,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.

Loss of income during treatment period:
23.

PW1 has stated that, he was working as a Clerk at Advocate office and earning Rs.25,000/-
per month.
He has not placed any iota of documents to show his income.
In the absence of the documents, it is apt to be considered notional income of the petitioner.

On going through the discharge summary marked at Ex.P9 & Ex.P10 shows that the petitioner was admitted from Rudresha D E vs Ksrtc on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92222954/
5 21.04.2023 to 02.05.2023 adn 31.05.2023 to 05.06.2023.

During the period of treatment, definitely,
there was some difficulty to him to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a period of two months by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.32,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

Medical Expeneses;
24.
The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses produced medical bills at Ex.P12 to the extent of Rs.4,53,592/- along with prescriptions at Ex.P13.
Except the suggestion there are no contra materials to show that the medical bills are created for the purpose of this case.

But on perusal of medial bills the Sl.No.27 of Rs.10,000/- is the advance receipt, Sl.No.63, assessment of Rs.200/-,
and Sl.No.69 of Rs.2,660/-.
After deducting the said amount it comes to Rs.4,40,732/-.
Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.4,40,732/- towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges;
25.

The petitioner herein, as per the medical records and also on going through the discharge summaries the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient and as an outpatient, definitely the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.20,000/-
towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

Loss of future income;
26.The petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P6 goes to show that, he had sustained grievous injuries for which he took the treatment as an inpatient.
Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr.Peddi Manjunath examined as PW2.
PW2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained Right leg is crush and degloving injury of skin around ankel and heal pad with fracture of medial malleolus and firth metatarsla.
X-ray shows fracture non-union of III metatarsal other fracture united.
He has assessed the disability 27% for particular limb.
27. At the time of cross-examination of PW2, stated that he is the treated doctor and also denied the suggestion that he assessed the disability of the petitioner on higher side.
28. Over all appreciation of evidence of PW2 along with the entire medical documents the disability expressed by PW2 as 27% for particular limb.
Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by PW2, it is apt to take whole body disability as 9%.
The same will meets the ends of justice.

Rudresha D E vs Ksrtc on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92222954/
6 29.
In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 45 years.

In support of the age proof,
he has placed DL marked at Ex.P19 for consideration.
On going through the said document, the date of birth of the petitioner has been mentioned as 04.07.1978.
The accident occurred on 21.04.2023.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is considered as 45 years.
To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '14' is to be taken into consideration.

30. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in his evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident he was working as a Clerk and getting an income of Rs.25,000/- per month.

To prove his income, the petiitoner has produced Letter issued by S,AnilKumar, Advocate stating the he is an Advocate practing at Civil Court and High Court Bangalore and petitioner has working in his office since 8 years and was given salary of Rs.25,000/-
p.m.,
But petitioner has not exmained the employer.
Apart from this he has not produced any oher document to show his income.
In the absence of the material documents, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, in the case on hand, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2023.

As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.16,000/- for the year 2023.
31.

In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood on going through his age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.16,000 X 12 X 14 X9/100= Rs.2,41,920/-.

Loss of amenities;
32.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accidental injuries he is unable to stand and unable to do his work as earlier.
On perusal of evidence of PW2 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood.

Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.20,000/-
towards loss of amenities.

Future Medical Expenses;
33.
PW2 has not stated about the future medication.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of future medication.

34. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
Compensation heads Compensation amount Rudresha D E vs Ksrtc on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92222954/
7 1.Pain and Suffering Rs. 60,000-00 2.Loss of income during Rs. 32,000-00 laid-up period and rest period 3.

Medical expenses Rs.4,40,732-00 4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 20,000-00 and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income Rs.2,41,920-00 due to disability 6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 20,000-00 7.Future medical expenses NIL Total Rs.8,14,652-00 35.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,14,652/- (Rupees eight lakh fourteen thousand six hundred and fifty two only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.
And MFA No.30131/2019 dated.12.5.2020, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount

LIABILITY:
36.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-37-F-0821 alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

In such a situation, the respondent No.2 being the owner cum internal insurance company of the offending vehicle KSRTC bus No.KA- 57-F-4997 is liable to pay the compensation determined by this court to the petitioner along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a.
from the date of the petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
37.

In view of above discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for  compensation of Rs.8,14,652/- (Rupees eight lakh fourteen thousand six hundred and fifty two only) along with interest @ 6% per annum,
from the date of the petition till the realization of the award amount.

Rudresha D E vs Ksrtc on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92222954/
8
The respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years and remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected by me and then pronounced in open court on this the 08th day of April 2025).
